Yeah, we should have been using about one reel of the good tape to get the guy's voice preserved, provided it's worth preserving, and then after that put it on the other tape, because this other tape lasts pretty good when it's air conditioned, I think. It used to go to pieces. I've had tapes that I've recorded. It's actually gone to pieces in seven or eight years' time. The life was only good for five years. We're going through the Jelly Roll Morton. I can't talk at all sometimes. The Jelly notes in my notebook. First of all, I have a lot of things copied, like that big letter he wrote, the downbeat, and also the Afro-American in Baltimore. When Handy wrote an article saying he had invented the blues, and Jelly told him he'd heard more blues back here on the old junk man's horn than Handy would ever know. Incidentally, Johnny Wiggs' interview, he raved about those junk men, which I guess we'll never get to know now.…
